lee: Heads-up — after rolling kernel-selector v2 onto TP shards for fp8 models we saw a ~25% throughput drop on multi-GPU 32k context runs. Not a single-node bug, fleet-wide on 8/16 TP configs.

sara: ugh, noticed some regression alerts this morning. Any quick repro?

lee: Repro steps I ran: `python infra/bench/run_inference.py --model redwood-34b-fp8 --tp 8 --pp 2 --batch 4 --micro 8 --context 32768 --warmup 10 --steps 50`
Baseline (kernel v1): 9500 tokens/s. With selector v2: 7200 tokens/s.

vikram: Can you paste a short profile? nvprof/nsys/snaps?

lee: Uploaded a light nsys trace to S3: https://s3.redwood/prof/1782103456/nsys.zip (perf-bot also posted summary)

perf-bot: Profile summary: allreduce time increased from 9% -> 22% of step; idle/wait on CUDA stream rose ~180ms; GEMM kernels show longer P95. Kernel names: `cutlass_gemm_fp8_kernel_v2` vs `cutlass_gemm_fp8_kernel_v1`.

emily: Interesting — selector v2 picks a new cutlass path that fuses matmul+transpose for perf on single-GPU shapes, but maybe it hurts TP because it changes scheduling of compute/comm.

lee: Exact suspicion. v2 emits larger contiguous ops that block the stream where we previously overlapped asynchronous all-reduce. The NVTX timeline shows all-reduce launches later.

vikram: Also check KV cache behavior: any extra memcpy/packing between TP shards? We recently changed KV packing alignment in PR #4122 to pad up to 128 bytes for cutlass v2. That could cause extra memcpy across shards.

lee: Good call. The trace shows extra `kv_pack` memcpy calls right before sharded send. Those were negligible on single-GPU but now cause a serialized copy on the owner rank.

sara: So two compounding effects: (1) kernel v2 increases compute burst and delays all-reduce launch; (2) kv_pack padding adds synchronous memcpy/copy before NCCL send. Together they kill comm/compute overlap.

emily: Can we try: (A) force kernel selector back to v1 for TP runs, (B) disable kv_pack padding, (C) toggle prefer_streamed_allreduce in runtime? Quick A/B should isolate main culprit.

lee: I ran A and C locally. Forcing v1 restored to ~9400 tokens/s. Setting `prefer_streamed_allreduce=false` on v2 recovered to ~8800 tokens/s (partial). Disabling kv_pack padding in isolation recovered ~9200. All three together brought performance back to baseline.

vikram: That nails it. Primary culprit is scheduling mismatch (v2), secondary is padding-induced serialize.

emily: Any numeric breakdown you can paste? Even rough percentages.

lee: Sure — rough averages over 50 steps (8 TP, 2 PP):
- baseline (v1, no padding): 9500 tokens/s, allreduce 9%
- v2 + padding: 7200 tokens/s, allreduce 22%
- v2 + prefer_streamed_allreduce=false: 8800 tokens/s, allreduce 15%
- v2 + no padding: 9200 tokens/s, allreduce 11%
- v2 + no padding + prefer_streamed_allreduce=false: 9400 tokens/s, allreduce 10%

sara: Good. Next steps? Rollback selector v2 on multi-gpu fleet? Or add a runtime guard for TP shapes?

vikram: Add a runtime rule: for TP shards and aggregated KV sizes > 16MB, prefer `cutlass_gemm_fp8_kernel_v1`. Also revert the padding change until we land an async pack path.

emily: I'll open quick PRs: (1) runtime selector guard, (2) revert kv padding + add async pack ticket. Also add a micro-benchmark to catch comm/compute overlap regressions in CI.

lee: I'm going to schedule an A/B rollback for the affected rollout group (fleet tag: tp-v2-202603). Rollback if >10% regression.

sara: Can we add telemetry: %allreduce_time per request and kv_memcpy_count tagged by tp/pp config so we detect this class earlier?

vikram: Yes — telemetry plugin already captures allreduce_ms and memcpy_ms; will add a tp/pp dimension and kv_pack_count. Patch incoming.

perf-bot: Perf alert created: INC-2026-1782 (regression in tp kernel selector). Linked to trace: https://s3.redwood/prof/1782103456/nsys.zip

emily: FYI — FP8 scaling note: I saw some int-accum saturation warnings in log when running v2 + larger batch sizes; may need to clamp scale or fallback to fp16 accumulation for tall matmuls. Filed as follow-up.

lee: Good catch — add that to the ticket. For now the mitigation path is clear. I'll push the runtime guard + telemetry and coordinate rollback.

sara: Thanks everyone — quick and effective triage. :thumbsup:
